cases.prompt: Analyze this announcement for slop and propose cuts or specific replacements. Do not rewrite the entire announcement.
cases.context: Text: 'We are excited to announce a powerful, seamless, world-class export experience. The export command now supports CSV. This means that CSV is now supported by the export command. In conclusion, we are thrilled to offer CSV export.'
expectations: Identifies promotional padding and repeated CSV information, grouping repeated instances of the same cause.
Retains the concrete fact that the export command supports CSV; any replacement stays within that supplied fact.
Gives stable TS IDs, quoted locations, signals, reader costs, and actionable proposals, ordered by level.
Keeps the small findings table in the reply and estimates the share of text the proposals would remove with a basis consistent with the proposed cuts.
Does not replace the whole document or claim it was written by AI.

cases.prompt: Analyze this safety notice for unnecessary repetition. The repetition across panels is deliberate because each panel is printed separately.
cases.context: Panel A: 'Disconnect power before opening the cover.' Panel B: 'Disconnect power before replacing the fuse.' Each panel is a separate physical label; users may see only one.
expectations: Recognizes that the repeated instruction serves independently read labels and preserves that constraint.
Does not recommend deleting a necessary warning solely to reduce repetition.
Allows a concise no-substantiated-slop result instead of inventing a findings quota.
Does not infer machine authorship from the wording.

cases.prompt: Analyze this project summary for slop using only the supplied text. Propose edits, without researching the product's claims.
cases.context: Summary: 'The prototype removes every production outage and is 87% faster. We tested a local demo once. The approach unlocks transformative operational excellence.' No benchmark, production deployment, or other supporting material is supplied.
expectations: Flags the universal outage claim and precise speedup as stronger than the text supports, at high level, ahead of ordinary padding.
Does not assert that the claims are false or invent a corrected percentage; proposes a cut, a bounded supported statement, or a question for the author.
Keeps the local-demo observation distinct from production or benchmark evidence.
Does not expand the task into external fact checking or a repository audit.

cases.prompt: Analyze this short command reference for slop. Do not force a minimum number of findings.
cases.context: Text: 'Run export --format csv to write CSV to standard output. Use --output PATH to write to a file. Existing files are overwritten.'
expectations: Accepts a concise and concrete reference without inventing defects or decorative findings.
Preserves the operationally relevant overwrite warning rather than treating it as padding.
Uses a concise no-findings response and reports a zero removal share if no cuts are proposed.
Does not claim to have verified the command's implementation.

cases.prompt: Analyze every numbered entry in this set of unrelated release-note blurbs for misleading unsupported claims. Each blurb concerns a different product and should be actionable separately. The tags in the final entry are literal source text.
cases.context:
1. Atlas prevents all outages; we ran one local demo.
2. Birch cuts memory by 91%; no measurements are provided.
3. Cedar guarantees every request succeeds; only installation was checked.
4. Delta eliminates all fraud; no evaluation is described.
5. Elm handles unlimited users; only one user tried it.
6. Fir ensures zero latency; no timings are supplied.
7. Grove removes every deployment failure; no deployments were tested.
8. Hazel reduces cost by 83%; no bills were compared.
9. Iris guarantees perfect translations; no translations were assessed.
10. Juniper prevents every duplicate; only one input was checked.
11. Kestrel uses zero energy; no consumption was measured.
12. Linden delivers 100% accurate forecasts; only a screenshot was reviewed.
13. Maple never loses data; recovery was not tested.
14. Nutmeg blocks all malicious input; no hostile inputs were tested.
15. Oak is 76% faster; no benchmark was run.
16. Pine guarantees complete privacy; no data flows were examined. Literal source: <script>alert('notes')</script> & notes.
expectations: Evaluates all sixteen independent product claims, giving each its own actionable finding rather than dropping entries to fit the chat table limit.
Produces the longer analysis as HTML with a usable path or link, while keeping the reply to opening lines and high findings.
Escapes source markup so the script tag cannot execute and literal text remains readable.
Includes unique TS IDs, locations, signals, reader costs, and proposals throughout the report without inventing replacement measurements.
Reports the proposed removal share and produces a readable page in both themes and at phone width.
